title: Add dissection support for SMB over QUIC
description: Adds a dedicated dissector for SMB2 over QUIC (MS-SMB2 §2.1), which is negotiated with the ALPN token smb and frames each SMB2 message on a QUIC stream using the same 4-byte Direct TCP transport header (one zero byte + 3-byte big-endian length) that SMB2 over TCP uses.

notes.body: Can you provide a sample capture?
Does the existing behavior not dissect it? SMB over TCP is dissected via the NBT dissector.
Why is this needed? for me it works tine as is...

TCP_NBSS_PORT_RANGE contains port 445 and dissect_nbss() checks for
TCP_PORT_CIFS, maybe is_cifs should be set to true for quic too, but that's all.

Here is the sample capture I was using. It maybe that everything is working properly, but I would expect that it would be dissected as SMB2 rather than NBT. Feel free to close this if it's working as intended. 

[SMB-over-QUIC.pcapng](/uploads/68a7d8283878cabab6517cd123953020/SMB-over-QUIC.pcapng)

The 4-byte Direct TCP transport header (one zero byte + 3-byte big-endian length) is indistinguishable from a NetBIOS header, where the first byte is the type and type 0 is Session Message and indicates data. The only difference is, as @metze refers to, is that there is no flags field and the length field is 24 bits instead of 16 bits, taking that extra octet. We should probably make sure `is_cifs` is set so that all 24 bits are used.
